judgments.yea_description: Voted for S. 316, which repealed the 1991 and 2002 laws allowing military force against Iraq, withdrawing the standing legal basis for military action there. The Senate passed it 66-30.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against S. 316, which repealed the 1991 and 2002 laws allowing military force against Iraq, withdrawing the standing legal basis for military action there. The Senate passed it 66-30.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.J.Res. 27 to cancel the federal rule defining which streams and wetlands are protected as waters of the United States under the Clean Water Act. The Senate passed it 53-43.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.J.Res. 27 to cancel the federal rule defining which streams and wetlands are protected as waters of the United States under the Clean Water Act. The Senate passed it 53-43.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1, the Lower Energy Costs Act, which expanded oil, gas, and mineral production on federal land, sped up permitting and environmental review for energy projects, and repealed several climate program fees. The House passed it 225-204.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1, the Lower Energy Costs Act, which expanded oil, gas, and mineral production on federal land, sped up permitting and environmental review for energy projects, and repealed several climate program fees. The House passed it 225-204.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 734, the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, which broke Title IX, the school civil rights law, by letting anyone whose sex at birth was male play on a women's or girls' team. The House passed it 219-203.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 734, the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, which broke Title IX, the school civil rights law, by letting anyone whose sex at birth was male play on a women's or girls' team. The House passed it 219-203.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for S.J.Res. 11 to cancel the federal environmental agency rule tightening nitrogen oxide and other emission standards for new heavy-duty trucks and engines. The Senate passed it 50-49.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against S.J.Res. 11 to cancel the federal environmental agency rule tightening nitrogen oxide and other emission standards for new heavy-duty trucks and engines. The Senate passed it 50-49.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for S.J.Res. 9 to cancel the Fish and Wildlife Service rule listing the lesser prairie-chicken as threatened and endangered, removing its Endangered Species Act protection. The Senate passed it 50-48.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against S.J.Res. 9 to cancel the Fish and Wildlife Service rule listing the lesser prairie-chicken as threatened and endangered, removing its Endangered Species Act protection. The Senate passed it 50-48.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for S.J.Res. 24 to cancel the Fish and Wildlife Service rule listing the northern long-eared bat as endangered, removing its Endangered Species Act protection. The Senate passed it 51-49.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against S.J.Res. 24 to cancel the Fish and Wildlife Service rule listing the northern long-eared bat as endangered, removing its Endangered Species Act protection. The Senate passed it 51-49.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 2, which restarted border wall construction, sharply narrowed asylum eligibility, restricted temporary entry permission and protections for children who arrive alone, and required employers nationwide to use E-Verify. The House passed it 219-213.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 2, which restarted border wall construction, sharply narrowed asylum eligibility, restricted temporary entry permission and protections for children who arrive alone, and required employers nationwide to use E-Verify. The House passed it 219-213.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for S.J.Res. 18 to cancel the 2022 public-benefit rule for green cards, reinstating the stricter 2019 standard that counted use of benefits such as Medicaid and food assistance against an immigrant seeking a green card. The Senate passed it 50-47.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against S.J.Res. 18 to cancel the 2022 public-benefit rule for green cards, reinstating the stricter 2019 standard that counted use of benefits such as Medicaid and food assistance against an immigrant seeking a green card. The Senate passed it 50-47.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 2494, which made assaulting a law enforcement officer, firefighter, or other first responder grounds to remove any noncitizen from the country. The House passed it 255-175.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 2494, which made assaulting a law enforcement officer, firefighter, or other first responder grounds to remove any noncitizen from the country. The House passed it 255-175.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for sending S.J.Res. 11 to the President to cancel the federal environmental agency rule tightening nitrogen oxide and other emission standards for new heavy-duty trucks and engines. The House passed it 221-203.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against sending S.J.Res. 11 to the President to cancel the federal environmental agency rule tightening nitrogen oxide and other emission standards for new heavy-duty trucks and engines. The House passed it 221-203.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.J.Res. 45 to cancel the Education Department rule that paused federal student loan payments and cancelled up to $20,000 of debt per borrower. The House passed it 218-203.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.J.Res. 45 to cancel the Education Department rule that paused federal student loan payments and cancelled up to $20,000 of debt per borrower. The House passed it 218-203.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 467, the HALT Fentanyl Act, which permanently put fentanyl-related substances in the strictest federal drug category and gave them the same trafficking penalties as fentanyl. The House passed it 289-133.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 467, the HALT Fentanyl Act, which permanently put fentanyl-related substances in the strictest federal drug category and gave them the same trafficking penalties as fentanyl. The House passed it 289-133.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for sending H.J.Res. 45 to the President to cancel the Education Department rule that paused federal student loan payments and cancelled up to $20,000 of debt per borrower. The Senate passed it 52-46.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against sending H.J.Res. 45 to the President to cancel the Education Department rule that paused federal student loan payments and cancelled up to $20,000 of debt per borrower. The Senate passed it 52-46.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.J.Res. 44 to cancel the federal firearms agency rule treating pistols fitted with stabilizing braces as short-barreled rifles subject to stricter registration. The House passed it 219-210.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.J.Res. 44 to cancel the federal firearms agency rule treating pistols fitted with stabilizing braces as short-barreled rifles subject to stricter registration. The House passed it 219-210.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1615, the Gas Stove Protection and Freedom Act, which barred the Consumer Product Safety Commission from banning gas stoves or issuing a safety standard that would substantially restrict their use. The House passed it 248-180.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1615, the Gas Stove Protection and Freedom Act, which barred the Consumer Product Safety Commission from banning gas stoves or issuing a safety standard that would substantially restrict their use. The House passed it 248-180.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1640, the Save Our Gas Stoves Act, which blocked the Department of Energy from setting efficiency standards for kitchen ranges and ovens that would push consumers away from gas models. The House passed it 249-181.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1640, the Save Our Gas Stoves Act, which blocked the Department of Energy from setting efficiency standards for kitchen ranges and ovens that would push consumers away from gas models. The House passed it 249-181.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.J.Res. 44, which would cancel the federal firearms agency rule treating pistols fitted with stabilizing braces as short-barreled rifles subject to stricter registration. The Senate rejected it 49-50, so it did not become law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.J.Res. 44, which would cancel the federal firearms agency rule treating pistols fitted with stabilizing braces as short-barreled rifles subject to stricter registration. The Senate rejected it 49-50, so it did not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 3941, the Schools Not Shelters Act, which barred federally funded schools and colleges from housing immigrants who entered without legal permission. The House passed it 222-201.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 3941, the Schools Not Shelters Act, which barred federally funded schools and colleges from housing immigrants who entered without legal permission. The House passed it 222-201.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for sending S.J.Res. 9 to the President to cancel the Fish and Wildlife Service rule listing the lesser prairie-chicken as threatened and endangered, removing its Endangered Species Act protection. The House passed it 221-206.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against sending S.J.Res. 9 to the President to cancel the Fish and Wildlife Service rule listing the lesser prairie-chicken as threatened and endangered, removing its Endangered Species Act protection. The House passed it 221-206.
